question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{6})=-\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{4}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{7\pi }{6} & =-\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x-\frac{7\pi }{6} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{11\pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{11\pi }{12}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{(4n+1)\pi }{4} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(12n+11)\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{4}$ and $x=\frac{23\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$  So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{4},\,\frac{11\pi }{12},\,\frac{5\pi }{4},\,\frac{23\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{4}=\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \frac{23\pi }{12}=\frac{23{\pi }^{2}}{48}.
$$
